e-7663.worked_solution:
When we have an inequality involving an exponential function with a positive base, we're allowed to multiply or divide both sides by the exponential function.

Multiplying both sides of the given inequality by $11^x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{({x}^{2}-8)^{3}}{{11}^{x}} & \ge 0 \\ {11}^{x}\cdot \frac{({x}^{2}-8)^{3}}{{11}^{x}} & \ge {11}^{x}\cdot 0 \\ ({x}^{2}-8)^{3} & \ge 0.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can solve the inequality using familiar methods:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt[3]{({x}^{2}-8)^{3}} & \ge \sqrt[3]{0} \\ {x}^{2}-8 & \ge 0 \\ {x}^{2} & \ge 8 \\ \sqrt{{x}^{2}} & \ge \sqrt{8} \\ |x| & \ge 2\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the inequality is $x \leq -2\sqrt 2$ or $x \geq 2 \sqrt 2.$

First, we move all the terms to the left side of the inequality and factor:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}\cdot {2}^{2x-7} & \ge {2}^{2x-3} \\ {x}^{2}\cdot {2}^{2x-7}-{2}^{2x-3} & \ge 0 \\ ({x}^{2}-{2}^{4})\cdot {2}^{2x-7} & \ge 0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we divide both sides by ${2}^{2x-7}$ and get

$$
{x}^{2}-{2}^{4}\ge 0.
$$

Finally, we can solve this inequality using familiar methods:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-{2}^{4} & \ge 0 \\ {x}^{2} & \ge 16 \\ \sqrt{{x}^{2}} & \ge \sqrt{16} \\ |x| & \ge 4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the inequality is $x\le -4$ or $x\ge 4.$
